CVE-2026-12725.title: A heap-based buffer overflow was found in dnsmasq. When DNSSEC va ...
CVE-2026-12725.description:
A heap-based buffer overflow was found in dnsmasq. When DNSSEC validation and
query logging are both enabled, logging of DS or DNSKEY replies containing
unsupported algorithm or digest types can cause dnsmasq to write past the end
of an internal logging buffer. A remote attacker able to supply such a DNS
response may crash the dnsmasq process, resulting in denial of service.

CVE-2026-12969.title: An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in dnsmasq's find_soa( ...
CVE-2026-12969.description: An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in dnsmasq's find_soa() function in src/rfc1035.c. When parsing NS section records, extract_name() is called with extrabytes=0, failing to validate that 10 additional bytes exist for fixed-length DNS record fields. A remote attacker controlling a DNS zone can exploit this via a crafted NXDOMAIN response to cause a 10-byte heap out-of-bounds read, potentially accessing stale data from prior transactions.

CVE-2026-2291.title: dnsmasqs extract_name() function can be abused to cause a heap bu ...
CVE-2026-2291.description: dnsmasqs extract_name() function can be abused to cause a heap buffer overflow, allowing an attacker to inject false DNS cache entries, which could result in DNS lookups to redirect to an attacker-controlled IP address, or to cause a DoS.

CVE-2026-4890.title: A Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability in the DNSSEC validation  ...
CVE-2026-4890.description: A Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability in the DNSSEC validation of dnsmasq allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a crafted DNS packet.

CVE-2026-4891.title: A heap-based out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the DNSSEC valid ...
CVE-2026-4891.description: A heap-based out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the DNSSEC validation of dnsmasq allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a crafted DNS packet.

CVE-2026-4892.title: A heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the DHCPv6 impl ...
CVE-2026-4892.description: A heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the DHCPv6 implementation of dnsmasq allows local attackers to execute arbitrary code with root privileges via a crafted DHCPv6 packet.

CVE-2026-4893.title: An information disclosure vulnerability in dnsmasq allows remote  ...
CVE-2026-4893.description: An information disclosure vulnerability in dnsmasq allows remote attackers to bypass source checks via a crafted DNS packet with RFC 7871 client subnet information.

CVE-2026-5172.title: A buffer overflow in dnsmasq’s extract_addresses() function allow ...
CVE-2026-5172.description: A buffer overflow in dnsmasq’s extract_addresses() function allows an attacker to trigger a heap out-of-bounds read and crash by exploiting a malformed DNS response, enabling extract_name() to advance the pointer past the record’s end.

CVE-2026-6507.title: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. A remote attacker could exploit an o ...
CVE-2026-6507.description: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. A remote attacker could exploit an out-of-bounds write vulnerability by sending a specially crafted BOOTREPLY (Bootstrap Protocol Reply) packet to a dnsmasq server configured with the `--dhcp-split-relay` option. This can lead to memory corruption, causing the dnsmasq daemon to crash and resulting in a denial of service (DoS).

CVE-2026-93006.title: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. The TFTP server can serve the wrong  ...
CVE-2026-93006.description: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. The TFTP server can serve the wrong file contents because a recently used transfer cache is not invalidated when a transfer finishes. An attacker on the local network who can request a TFTP file may cause a later client to receive previously cached data instead of the requested file. In PXE network-boot environments this can substitute attacker-chosen boot content for a victim machine.

CVE-2026-93007.title: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. The TCP DNS service uses a small fix ...
CVE-2026-93007.description: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. The TCP DNS service uses a small fixed pool of child processes and does not set a receive timeout on client connections. A remote attacker can open idle TCP connections to port 53 and occupy the entire pool, preventing new TCP DNS connections and DNSSEC validation that requires TCP fallback. UDP DNS resolution continues, and occupied slots are released after a fixed lifetime.

CVE-2026-93008.title: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. When following a CNAME in a DNS resp ...
CVE-2026-93008.description: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. When following a CNAME in a DNS response, the resolver can cache records for the CNAME target without checking that those records belong to the responding server's authorized zone. In split-DNS deployments that send some domains to a specific upstream, an attacker who controls that upstream can inject cache entries for unrelated names. Later clients may then receive attacker-chosen addresses for those names.

CVE-2026-93009.title: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. The DHCPv6 client hostname parser ca ...
CVE-2026-93009.description: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. The DHCPv6 client hostname parser can read one byte past the end of a crafted FQDN option because it checks the next label length before confirming the pointer is still inside the option. An attacker on the local network can trigger this with a single DHCPv6 packet. The extra byte is not returned to the client or logged, and no crash has been demonstrated.

CVE-2026-93010.title: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. When DHCP leasequery is enabled with ...
CVE-2026-93010.description: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. When DHCP leasequery is enabled without listing allowed source addresses, the server does not check who sent the query. A host on the local network can request DHCP lease records and learn assigned addresses, MAC addresses, hostnames, and related lease metadata. The feature is off unless an administrator turns it on.

CVE-2026-93011.title: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. After a reduction of internal domain ...
CVE-2026-93011.description: A flaw was found in dnsmasq. After a reduction of internal domain-name buffer sizes, the DNSSEC validator can write a few bytes past a name buffer when converting names to and from DNS wire format. An attacker who can cause the server to validate a crafted DNSSEC response may overwrite a small amount of adjacent heap metadata. DNSSEC support is not compiled in by default and must also be enabled at runtime.
